• Presence of **Anti-HBs** with the absence of all other serological virus markers indicates **immunity** following **HBV vaccination.**

• **Postvaccination testing** for the presence of anti-HBs is **not recommended** for infants, children, and most adults. • **HBV "escape" mutants** in which the HBsAg is altered can result in HBV infections without detectable anti-HBs.

question_stem.text: Which of the following is the most common cause of post-transfusion hepatitis in developed countries?
question_stem.markdown: Which of the following is the most common cause of post-transfusion hepatitis in developed countries?

peer_accuracy_statement: 48% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
The most common cause of **post-transfusion hepatitis** in developed countries is **Hepatitis C.**

**Hepatitis C infection** is mainly by blood transfusion and other modes of contact with infected blood or blood products. Injectable drug abusers, transplant recipients, and immunocompromised persons are at high risk.

The **most common** serious complication of **blood transfusion** is **post-transfusion hepatitis** from the **hepatitis C virus (HCV).**

**Vertical transmission** also takes place.

Note: Although hepatitis B (HBV) is a highly infective virus, the introduction of routine donor screening for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) reduced cases of PTH in the developed countries by about a third. Furthermore, active immunization with hepatitis B vaccine has markedly reduced the incidence of transfusion transmitted hepatitis B infection.

images.caption: Schematic diagram of the Hepatitis B virus replication cycle showing entry, nuclear cccDNA formation, pregenomic RNA transcription, HBx transcription activator, reverse transcription in viral cores, ER assembly, and release
images.visual_description: Color diagram of a host hepatocyte ('cytoplasm' and 'nucleus') illustrating the Hepatitis B virus life cycle: 'viral particle' -> 'entry' -> 'virus core' -> nuclear 'covalently closed circular viral DNA' ('HBx transcription activator') -> 'pregenomic RNA' and 'mRNA' -> 'ribosomes' -> 'ER' -> 'assembly' -> 'release' of 'viral particles' (and intracellular 'recycling' of cores back to the nucleus).

explanation_markdown:
The given life cycle is of hepatitis virus.

• The infectious virion attaches to cells and becomes uncoated.
• In the nucleus, the partially double-stranded viral genome is converted to covalently closed circular double- stranded DNA (cccDNA).
• The cccDNA serves as template for all viral transcripts, including a 3.5-kb pregenome RNA.
• The pregenome RNA becomes encapsidated with newly synthesized HBcAg.
• Within the cores, the viral polymerase synthesizes by reverse transcription a negative-strand DNA copy.
• The polymerase starts to synthesize the positive DNA strand, but the process is not completed.
• Cores bud from the pre-Golgi membranes, acquiring HBsAg-containing envelopes, and may exit the cell.
• Alternatively, cores may be re-imported into the nucleus and initiate another round of replication in the same cell.

peer_accuracy_statement: 50% of the people got this right

**Subtype C** viruses are the **most common form** in India and in the world. More than 95% of infections in India, home to an estimated 2.1 million HIV-infected individuals, are of **subtype C.**

There are 4 **groups** of HIV-1: **M (Major), N (non-M, non-O), O** (outlier) and **P** (Putative).

Among these, group M is responsible for most of the infections. **The M group** comprises of nine subtypes designated as A, B, C, D, F, G, H, J, and K.

• **vif:** Viral infectivity factor gene
• **vpu: (only in HIV-1)** and **vpx (only in HIV-2)**

question_stem.markdown: Which of the following statements is false regarding HIV?

options.text: Male-to-female HIV transmission is usually more efficient in causing infection than female-to-male transmission
The risk of HIV acquisition associated with unprotected receptive anal intercourse is lower than that seen in penile-vaginal intercourse
The quantity of HIV-1 in plasma is a primary determinant of the risk of HIV-1 transmission

peer_accuracy_statement: 59% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
The risk of HIV acquisition associated with **unprotected receptive anal intercourse** is **relatively higher** than that seen in penile-vaginal intercourse.

This may be due to the reason that only a thin, **fragile rectal mucosal membrane** separates the deposited semen from potentially susceptible cells in and beneath the mucosa, and also the **micro-trauma** of the mucosal membrane may be associated with anal intercourse.

The differences in transmission rates between men and women are because of the **prolonged exposure** of the **vaginal and cervical mucosa** as well as the endometrium to infected **seminal fluid.** However, the penis and urethral orifice are exposed relatively briefly to infected vaginal fluid.

question_stem.text: Which of the following statements is false regarding replication and pathogenesis of HIV?
question_stem.markdown: Which of the following statements is false regarding replication and pathogenesis of HIV?

options.text: The period of preintegration latency may last for hours to days
Pyroptosis is due to the enzyme caspase-1
Loss of plasma membrane integrity due to viral budding is considered an indirect mechanism in CD4 dysfunction

peer_accuracy_statement: 35% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
**Loss of plasma membrane integrity** due to viral budding is a **direct mechanism** involved in the CD4+ T Cell Dysfunction and Depletion.

**Preintegration latency:**

It is a phase in which **HIV** enters a **resting CD4+ T cell** and in the absence of an activation signal, reverse transcription of the HIV genome occurs to a limited extent but the resulting proviral DNA fails to integrate into the host genome. This period of **preintegration latency** may last hours to days, and if no activation signal is delivered to the cell, the **unintegrated DNA** undergoes **degradation** and loses its capacity to initiate a productive infection.

**Pyroptosis:**

• The phenomenon of **pyroptosis** is an inflammatory form of cell death involving the up regulation of the proinflammatory enzyme **caspase-1** and release of the proinflammatory cytokine **IL-1 β**, and it is linked to a bystander effect of HIV replication on CD4+ T cells.
• Apoptosis is seen in **"bystander" cells** such as **CD8+ T cells** and **B cells** as well as in **uninfected CD4+ T cells.**
• The intensity of apoptosis correlates with the general state of activation of the immune system and not with the stage of disease or with the viral burden.

question_stem.text: The first antibodies to be detected by ELISA or Western blot in an HIV patient are those against______
question_stem.markdown: The first antibodies to be detected by ELISA or Western blot in an HIV patient are those against______

peer_accuracy_statement: 18% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
The first antibodies to be detected are those directed against the immunodominant region of the envelope **gp41.**

Antibodies to HIV usually appear within 3–6 weeks and almost invariably within 12 weeks of primary infection. The appearance of **HIV-binding antibodies** detected by ELISA and Western blot assays occurs prior to the appearance of **neutralizing antibodies.**

The only viral proteins that elicit **neutralizing antibodies** are the envelope proteins **gp120 and gp41.**

The order of appearance of antibodies is as follows:

Envelope gp41 > gag protein (p24 and p55) >envelope gp120 >gag protein p17 > pol gene products (p31 and p66).

question_stem.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the diagnosis of HIV?
question_stem.markdown: Which of the following statements is true regarding the diagnosis of HIV?

options.text: Western blot demonstrating antibodies to products of all three of the major genes of HIV (gag, pol, and env) is conclusive evidence of infection with HIV
If the Western blot for HIV-1 is indeterminate, HIV-1 can be ruled out

peer_accuracy_statement: 38% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
Answer: **Western blot** demonstrating antibodies to products of all three of the major **genes of HIV** (gag, pol, and env) is conclusive **evidence of infection** with HIV.

Western blot result is considered positive if antibodies exist to two of the three HIV proteins: p24, gp41, and gp120/160.

Other options:

• Western blot patterns of reactivity that do not fall into the positive or negative categories are considered **indeterminate.**
• If the western blot for **HIV-1 is indeterminate**, it should be repeated in 4–6 weeks; in addition, one may proceed to a **p24 antigen capture assay, HIV-1 RNA assay**, or **HIV-1 DNA PCR** and specific serologic testing for **HIV-2.**
• HIV infection is associated with **thrombocytopenia**, not thrombocytosis.

The parameters that help establish immunodeficiency in HIV infection:

• Total leukocyte and lymphocyte count to demonstrate leucopenia and a lymphocyte count usually below 2000/mm³
• Absolute CD4+T cell count will be less than 200/mm³
• CD4: CD8 cell ratio reversed
• Thrombocytopenia
• Raised IgG and IgA levels
• Diminished CMI

Patients with PCP generally present with fever and a cough that is usually **non-productive** or productive of only scant amounts of white sputum.

The most common finding on chest x-ray is either a normal film if the disease is suspected early, or a **faint bilateral interstitial infiltrates.** The classic finding of **a dense perihilar infiltrate is unusual in patients with AIDS.**

The standard treatment for PCP or disseminated pneumocystosis is **trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole.**

pearls.title: Rabies vaccines and immunoglobulins (WHO guidelines)
pearls.body_text:
According to WHO [April 2018]:

[Image: MA7901_exp_img_1]

Individuals with **WHO** category II or III exposures should receive PEP without delay.

One **ID** dose is **0.1 mL** of vaccine and one **IM** dose is an **entire vial** of vaccine, irrespective of the vial size.

Should a vaccine dose be delayed for any reason, the PEP schedule should be resumed (not restarted).

**Rabies Immunoglobulin(RIG):**
• RIG provides a passive immunization and is administered only once, as soon as possible after the initiation of PEP and not beyond 7 days after the first dose of vaccine.
• Vaccines should never be withheld regardless of the availability of RIG.
• Max dose: **hRIG- 20IU/kg , eRIG-40IU/kg**
• All of the rabies immunoglobulin, or as much as anatomically possible (but avoiding possible compartment syndrome), should be administered into or around the wound site or sites. The remaining immunoglobulin, if any, should be injected intramuscularly at a site distant from the site of vaccine administration. Rabies immunoglobulin may be diluted to a volume sufficient for all wounds to be effectively and safely infiltrated.
• Prioritization of RIG allocation: Multiple bites>Deep wounds>Bites to head, neck and hands>Patients with severe immunodeficiency>The biting animal is confirmed or probable rabies>Bites, scratches, and exposure of mucous membranes caused by a bat.

**Immunodeficient individuals:** In the event of exposure a complete PEP course, including RIG is recommended irrespective of the PrEP status.

**(PrEP)Pre-exposure prophylaxis**
• PrEP considered in remote, rabies-endemic areas where access to PEP is difficult, the dog bite incidence is >5% per year or vampire bat rabies is known to be present.
• 2 sites ID or a 1-site IM vaccine administration on days 0 and 7.
• A routine PrEP booster or serology for neutralizing antibody titers is recommended only if a continued, high risk of rabies exposure remains.
• Individuals with documented immunodeficiency should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis and best receive an ID or IM PrEP schedule as above, plus a third vaccine administration between days 21 to 28.

question_stem.text: Which of the following statements is false regarding vaccination against Polio?
question_stem.markdown: Which of the following statements is false regarding vaccination against Polio?

options.text: Sabin type has the live attenuated virus
OPV is not allowed to be administered to immunocompromised persons
Salk type vaccine is associated with mutations that lead to reversal of virulence
Both OPV and IPV induces humoral IgG

peer_accuracy_statement: 35% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
**Salk type** is the **killed formalized vaccine,** hence there is no risk of mutation that can lead to a reversal of virulence like in OPV.

There are two types of vaccine that protect against polio: inactivated poliovirus vaccine **(IPV)** and oral poliovirus vaccine **(OPV).**

**Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) – Sabin:**

• OPV consists of a mixture of **live attenuated poliovirus strains** of each of the three serotypes. OPV used in India now contains only, **Type 1** and **Type 3.**
• The action of oral polio vaccine (OPV) is **two-pronged.** OPV produces antibodies in the blood (**'humoral' or serum immunity**) to all three types of poliovirus, and in the event of infection, this protects the individual against polio paralysis by preventing the spread of poliovirus to the nervous system.
• OPV strains also produce a **local immune response** in the lining ('mucous membrane') of the intestines - the primary site for poliovirus multiplication. The antibodies produced there **inhibit** the multiplication of **'wild' (naturally occurring) virus.** This intestinal immune response to OPV is a reason why mass campaigns with OPV have been shown to stop person-to-person transmission of wild poliovirus.

**Inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) – Salk:**

• IPV is produced from wild-type poliovirus strains of each serotype that have been **inactivated (killed)** with **formalin.**
• As an injectable vaccine, it can be administered alone or in combination with other vaccines (e.g., diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenza).
• Ideally, IPV should replace OPV as early as possible.
• Three doses of intramuscular IPV in primary series is the best option.
• Two doses of intramuscular IPV instead of three for primary series if started at 8 weeks, with an interval of 8 weeks between two doses is an alternative.
• In case IPV is not available or feasible, the child should be offered three doses of bOPV. In such cases, the child should be referred for two fractional doses of IPV at a Government facility at 6 and 14 weeks or at least one dose of intramuscular IPV, either standalone or as a combination vaccine, at 14 weeks of age.

question_stem.text: All are true about Zika virus except
question_stem.markdown: All are true about Zika virus except

options.text: Aedes aegypti is responsible for transmission of Zika virus
FDA approved diagnostic test for Zika virus is Trioplex rRT PCR
CSF sample is recommended in the first two months to detect virus RNA

peer_accuracy_statement: 54% of the people got this right
explanation_markdown:
CSF sample is NOT recommended in the first two months to detect viral RNA.

Zika virus RNA is generally detectable in **serum, whole blood and/or urine** during the acute phase of infection and up to **2 weeks** following the onset of symptoms, if present. A **urine sample is preferred in detecting congenital CMV infection via PCR**

Zika virus (RNA virus) is flavivirus. Aedes aegyti is responsible for the transmission.

However, sexual transmission is also observed **(Ebola virus** also is associated with **sexual transmission).**

Clinical symptoms are akin to Chikungunya. Zika virus infection is characterized by influenza-like clinical signs including **fever,** headache, and malaise.

A **maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis,** myalgia, and **arthralgia** usually accompany or follow those manifestations. **Petechial rashes are not seen.**

Complications: Guillian-Barre syndrome and microcephaly and intracranial calcification in infants born to mothers infected with Zika virus. Pregnant women should consider postponing travel to areas where Zika virus transmission is ongoing.

Diagnosis: Detecting viral RNA or neutralizing antibody.

The FDA has issued **Emergency Use Authorization** (EUA) for several diagnostic tools for Zika virus, which includes

  ◦ **Trioplex Real-Time RT-PCR (rRT-PCR) assay**
  ◦ **Zika MAC-ELISA.**

The Trioplex Real-Time RT-PCR Assay (Trioplex rRT-PCR-For detection of three viruses) is intended for the **qualitative detection and differentiation of RNA** from **Zika virus, dengue virus, and chikungunya virus** in human sera, whole blood (EDTA) or cerebrospinal fluid (each collected alongside a patient-matched serum specimen).

The test is also used for the qualitative detection of **Zika virus RNA in urine, and amniotic fluid.**

Negative Trioplex rRT-PCR results do not rule out dengue, chikungunya, and/or Zika virus infections and should not be used as the sole basis for patient management decisions.

explanation_markdown:
**Prions** are infectious agents composed entirely of a **protein material.** Prions composed of the **prion protein (PrP)** are believed to be the cause of **transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSEs)** among other diseases.

• Prions are the only known transmissible pathogens that are devoid of nucleic acid.
• Prion diseases may manifest as infectious, genetic, and sporadic disorders
• Prion diseases result from the accumulation of **PrP^Sc,** the conformation of which differs substantially from that of its precursor, **PrP^C.**
• Distinct strains of prions exhibit different biologic properties, which are epigenetically inherited.

**What are PrP^Sc and PrP^C ?**

• The specific protein that the prion is composed of is known as **the Prion Protein (PrP).**
• The **normal form** of the protein is called **PrP^C,** while the **infectious form** is called **PrP^Sc** – the **C** refers to **'cellular'** PrP, while the **Sc** refers to **'scrapie',** the prototypic prion disease, occurring in sheep.
• **Protease-resistant PrPSc-like protein (PrP^res)** is an isoform of PrP^C from which is structurally altered and converted into a misfolded proteinase K-resistant form in vitro.

explanation_markdown:
**Sporotrichosis:** It is caused by Sporothrix (Sporotrichum) schenckii.

• Sporothrix schenckii is a thermally dimorphic fungus that lives on vegetation.
• Following traumatic introduction into the skin, S schenckii causes sporotrichosis, a chronic granulomatous infection.
• The initial lesion develops as a granulomatous nodule that may progress to form a necrotic or ulcerative lesion.
• As the disease progresses it involves the cutaneous, subcutaneous and lymphatic tissue leading to the formation of **indolent ulcers** which are commonly encountered frequently among gardeners, forest workers, etc.
• From the lesions in the skin and subcutaneous tissue, the infection can spread via the lymphatic channels to the lymph nodes. This condition is known as **"lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis".**
